findings.title: traceID is dropped from the 'grafana-data-egress' log events
findings.body: The old LoggerMiddleware.logRequest explicitly appended `traceID` (from tracing.TraceIDFromContext) to the log params for the "Plugin Request Completed" / "grafana-data-egress" event. The new version removed that code and now relies on `m.logger.FromContext(ctx)` picking up contextual attributes, but the only attributes anyone adds to the context are `endpoint`, `pluginId`, `dsName`, `dsUID`, and `uname` (see ContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext). Nothing in this change adds the trace ID as a contextual attribute, so unless some other middleware injects it into the contextual logger, the data-egress audit log lines lose trace correlation with the request's span. If the intent was that FromContext supplies the trace ID automatically, that should be verified and covered by a test; otherwise the traceID field should be added in instrumentContext.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a throwaway logger, hiding logs from tests
findings.body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()`, a brand-new instance that is discarded. LoggerMiddleware now always logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` (logger_middleware.go line 58), so any test that injects a `*TestLogger` and asserts on `logger.InfoLogs` (Calls/Message/Ctx) will never see the "Plugin Request Completed" event — assertions will fail, or worse, tests will pass vacuously while the logging is broken. FromContext on the fake should return the receiver `f` (or otherwise record into `f`) so the existing fake remains usable to verify the middleware's new logging path.

findings.title: No tests for the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware or for log-field parity
findings.body: The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware (69 lines of new behavior) ships with no test file, and no test verifies that the LoggerMiddleware's output still contains the fields it used to log directly (pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName, dsUID, traceID). Since this refactor moved those fields from explicit log params to context attributes flowing between two middlewares, a regression in either the attribute injection or the middleware ordering would silently strip identifying fields from the grafana-data-egress audit log. A test asserting the full set of attributes on the resulting log line would catch this.

findings.title: LoggerMiddleware output now silently depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware being earlier in the chain
findings.body: LoggerMiddleware no longer includes pluginId/endpoint/uname/dsName/dsUID in its log output; those fields only appear if a ContextualLoggerMiddleware wrapped the client earlier in the stack (as done in pluginsintegration.CreateMiddlewares). Both `NewLoggerMiddleware` and `NewContextualLoggerMiddleware` are exported, so any caller that constructs the LoggerMiddleware on its own (e.g., Enterprise code or other middleware stacks built outside CreateMiddlewares) will emit 'grafana-data-egress' events with no plugin identification or endpoint. This ordering requirement is not documented on either constructor; at minimum a comment on NewLoggerMiddleware (and/or a debug safeguard) should state the dependency.
